extracted.intended_audience: Army public affairs officers (PAOs), Soldiers, Department of the Army civilians, and supporting contractors who create, review, post, or maintain Army public information (web sites, blogs, visual media, fund-raising publicity, and CE newspaper feasibility studies)
extracted.subtask_description: Official U.S. Army public affairs guidance for publishing information on official and unofficial web sites, blogs, visual materials, fund-raising publicity, awards entry standards, and conducting feasibility studies for civilian enterprise newspapers. Covers what may be published, clearance/training requirements, OPSEC/privacy constraints, and outreach/contracting procedures for CE newspapers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public information presumption and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: All information residing on a publicly accessible Web site is public information and is subject to the policies and clearance procedures listed in this regulation for releasing information to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official Web sites hosted, sponsored, or controlled by the U.S. Army must comply with AR 25–1, AR 25–2, AR 340–21, AR 380–5, AR 530–1, DODD 5230.09, DODI 5230.29, and JP 3–13. Information posted is potentially the official position of the DOD component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and editorial control of official Web sites
rubrics_metrics.description: An official Web site is a DOD Web site developed and maintained with command sponsorship and approval for which the DOD component (or subordinate organization/individual) exercises editorial control over content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content of official DOD Web sites is official in nature and may be endorsed as the official position of that DOD component; therefore approval and editorial control are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web site purpose and planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Each public Web site (or Web presence) must have a clearly defined purpose and Web site plan supporting the organization’s mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan should be approved by the organization’s commander or director and comply with review procedures in AR 25–1, paragraph 6–7. Sites should only post information of value to their visitors and commanders are encouraged to include social media in PA planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on nonreleasable information
rubrics_metrics.description: Official Web sites or Web logs (blogs) should not have any information that is considered nonreleasable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonreleasable information includes (but is not limited to): classified information; casualty information before next-of-kin verification; Privacy Act-protected data (age, DOB, home address, marital status, race); information about incidents under ongoing investigation; imagery/info of U.S. Coalition Forces without release; misrepresentations or statements conflicting with good order; sensitive photographs (IED strikes, battle scenes, casualties, destroyed/damaged equipment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Web site training requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PA officials responsible for posting unclassified information to official Web sites, regardless of domain, must complete the Web site training course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is offered through https://iatraining.us.army.mil and applies to Soldiers, DA civilians, and supporting contractors who review, post, and maintain Army content on non-Army.mil Web sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unofficial/personal Web site status
rubrics_metrics.description: Soldier and Government civilian-owned and maintained unofficial Web sites or blogs are created on personal time and not produced in connection with military or government duties or funded with DOD funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They are located on commercial networks (.com, .org, .biz, .edu, etc.) and generally require no advance clearance when produced in a personal capacity and not connected to official duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between free speech and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Government personnel using Internet technology should support individual freedom of speech and expression while demonstrating good order and discipline, reflecting Army Values, and safeguarding privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personnel must not make available personally identifiable information or operational security details of units/missions. Reasonable restrictions on free speech (e.g., no political commentary while in uniform) extend to electronic communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPSEC and protection of critical information
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals are responsible for protecting information to prevent adversaries from acquiring and using that information against the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When blogging/posting, personnel must ensure content does not violate disclosure of critical information; questions about sensitivity should be submitted for OPSEC and PA review prior to posting. Personnel must be cognizant of critical information examples provided in AR 530–1, annex C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and education
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders and other officials must hold personnel accountable for adherence to OPSEC regulations and applicable communications policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders must educate personnel on responsibilities and penalties for infractions so Government employees understand they are responsible for the content of their Web sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume global audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel should always assume that the entire world—adversaries, friendly, and neutrals alike—is viewing all transmitted or posted material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government employees are required to review all information and postings to ensure that the information posted will not put themselves, other employees, or their families at risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of Army Values
rubrics_metrics.description: Army personnel will ensure all writings and postings appropriately represent or convey the Army Values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to all internet postings, blogs, and electronic communications regardless of venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unofficial sites identifying Army affiliation must comply and disclaim
rubrics_metrics.description: Unofficial and personal Web sites in which individuals identify themselves as Soldiers or civilians affiliated with the U.S. Army must comply with local command policy and referenced policies, and must include a disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is the personal responsibility of personnel to ensure their personal Web sites do not contain nonreleasable information. A disclaimer must be added to preclude readers from assuming the site represents an Army position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on sensitive visual information
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not release imagery (digital, still, or video) of deceased, wounded, hospitalized, or detained personnel, or images of battle-damaged vehicles/equipment damaged by IEDs, direct enemy contact, or other enemy action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All visual information produced personally and provided to any media outlet, public Web site, family, or friends, whether in hard copy or electronic form, is subject to this regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irretrievability and permanence of web releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Once information has been released, it is irretrievable; information on the World Wide Web cannot be reliably targeted to only certain audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personnel should only post what they do not mind everyone viewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring of DOD computer systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Information placed on or sent over DOD computer systems is subject to monitoring, inspection, and audit by command or agency management at any time with or without notice or user consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes personal information, e-mail, personal user files/directories, and products created on DOD systems. Commanders are encouraged to implement additional guidance or restrictions based on technology, area of operation, atmospherics, or mission parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for officially authorized fund-raising publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: PA operations will support officially authorized fund-raising campaigns (for example, CFC) in accordance with AR 600–29 and this regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News coverage of the campaign will not discuss quotas, competition, or tallies of solicitation between or among agencies. To avoid appearance of endorsement, features and news coverage will discuss the campaign in general and focus on participation by command personnel, not specific agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund-raising event coverage standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Fund-raising events are covered through balanced, factual accounting of the campaign’s progress to include command or installation goals; such coverage is a normal news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage must not state, imply, or inspire existence of competition among units, offices, activities, or personnel to raise funds. Stories comparing unit participation or progress of subordinate units are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial content urging participation constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Content worded to urge participation in a fund-raising campaign (including editorials) will focus on the period of the campaign, the command’s position, and reader participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial opinion will not selectively benefit any organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Relations Award entry requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries for the Community Relations Award of Excellence should cover planning, execution, and results, and contain a summary of not more than two single-spaced, typed pages describing the program or event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries may be submitted by any person or organization at any time through command channels to the OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of the Spear Award nomination criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominees must have negated or seriously reduced potentially negative national and international publicity about Army issues, molded public opinion on controversial issues, or significantly enhanced positive public opinion about the Army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any Army employee may submit a written nomination through command channels to the CPA. Recipients determined by a selection board chaired by the CPA composed of senior PA officers, a senior civilian, and a senior NCO.

rubrics_metrics.name: MG Keith L. Ware competition entry standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries for the MG Keith L. Ware Public Affairs Communications Competition must meet the highest standards of production, presentation, execution, professional excellence, and originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A HQDA letter announces specific rules and categories; judges also consider awards for individual journalism categories (print and broadcast) and special distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CE newspaper feasibility study objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The feasibility study’s objective is to develop a list of qualified companies potentially interested in competing for a contract to print a civilian enterprise (CE) newspaper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Much of the data can be obtained from local installation and/or division personnel offices. The study is required by paras 3–5c and 3–5e(3)(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with contracting/SJA for CE study
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin the feasibility study by coordinating with the local contracting office and SJA and briefing the contracting office on the provisions of this regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform contracting that printers will be contacted to determine potential interest; invite contracting representative to meetings with printers; assure printers that appointments are informational and not solicitations for agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicizing potential CE contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: To publicize the potential CE newspaper contract to commercial sources, the contracting officer should announce it in the Commerce Business Daily and, where necessary, use press releases or advertisements in local newspapers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This develops commercial interest and informs potential bidders/printers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing a briefing for potential printers (mission statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief mission statement of the community and/or unit and the newspaper, explaining how the newspaper meets the interests and needs of the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sell the CE concept to printers by explaining 'what is in it for the CE printer' and include relevant market facts and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing a briefing for potential printers (demographics required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed market demographics including military population by grade categories (junior enlisted, senior enlisted, officers and RC/retirees), civilian population, total military and civilian payrolls, grade demographics with pay examples, children counts, local national employees (if overseas), number of family members, and geographic dispersion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use round figures; do not attempt to calculate taxes or allowances. If possible, provide data from local schools and break down demographics by grade ranges (E-1 to O-4+).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize purchasing power and captive market
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on purchasing power and emphasize that the paper reaches a captive market and offers exclusive distribution access to the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include other facts about where people shop, work, live, and relax, and conduct a resource study to define demographics and buying intentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify potential printers via multiple sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify potential printers through local Chambers of Commerce, business directories, the local contracting office, and by checking PX, commissary, library, and clubs for publications and printer names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile addresses and contact information for outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial contact and meeting practices with printers
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact printing representatives by phone or in person (face-to-face preferred) to indicate interest in meeting to discuss the possibility of producing the newspaper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If scheduling is successful, proceed to meeting procedures. If unsuccessful, document attempts (dates, times, brief descriptions) and forward through PAO channels to ACOM PAO; authorized funds for printing may be used only after documentation that a CE newspaper is not feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting conduct with printing representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: During meetings, inform the representative that the objective is to obtain information only and not to obtain an agreement; official specifications and contacts should be handled by the contracting office if a procurement proceeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not imply or lead printers to believe an agreement is being obtained during the informational meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation content and honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: When presenting to printers, show sample newspapers (including CE newspapers from other installations), explain differences, present demographics, and show printer profit potential, but do not mislead about circulation versus readership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful how information is presented (e.g., current press run vs total population). Discuss potential (more copies, exclusive distribution) and make printers aware that local official distribution channels can be used. Obtain case study information from other printers when possible.
